newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan doctors continue strike, despite deaths.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan doctors continue strike, despite deaths.

text.p: Venezuelan doctors pledged on Thursday to continue a strike over pay despite government reports that the stoppage has already caused six deaths.
"The medical conflict continues in its whole extent," Federation of Venezuelan Medics president Fernando Blanco said in a paid notice published in the local press.
Union representatives of Venezuela's 27,000 public doctors offered to return to work in emergency wards over the New Year's holiday period but that apparently lasted only a couple of days.
The strikers, who are seeking a nearly 1,000-percent pay increase, have said the government's intransigence was to blame for the six deaths reported since the movement began last Friday.

Labour Minister Juan Nepomuceno Garrido reiterated the government's stand not to negotiate with the striking doctors until they returned to work. "Not even in war time do you stop to treat the enemy," El Nacional newspaper quoted him as saying.
The paper said more than 100 women gave birth this week at Caracas Concepcion Palacios main maternity with only the help of nurses.
Overstretched military doctors and medical students are staffing emergency wards throughout the country.
Venezuelan doctors, who earn the equivalent of an average $126 a month, work in a public health system notoriously underfunded and poorly supplied.
